statement: A private company must not lodge a transfer of shares unless a proper instrument of transfer has been delivered to the company, and must lodge a notice of the transfer with the Registrar in the prescribed form; a transfer of any share in a private company on or after 3 January 2016 does not take effect until the Registrar updates the company's electronic register of members.
caveat: Like the allotment return, the filing is constitutive for private companies: ACRA's electronic register of members is the legal record, so a transfer has not happened until the register updates. Transfers also attract stamp duty on the instrument, payable through IRAS e-Stamping, and the constitution's transfer restrictions (the section 18 private-company requirement) govern whether the board may refuse registration (sections 128-129).
